cost: BOTH SUBJECTS LAND AT THE CEILING OF WHAT THIS LEVER CAN REACH, AND THE CEILING IS ARITHMETIC. The efficiency factor cannot exceed 1.00, so Jason Kidd '99's whole passer term is capped at 0.245 x playvol 94 x his gate 0.6627 = 15.26, his o_score at 76.51 and his OFF at 71 — the TOP of what any efficiency-side change can give him, and the bottom edge of 74 +-3. Kidd '02 is capped the same way at 73 against 75 +-3. A later round that wants their centres must open recal_117's VOLUME GATE, and that is where the conflict is: John Stockton '90 is volume 36 to Kidd '99's 38, the gate reads nothing else that separates them, he is pinned 84 +-3 and already reads 85. Every widening measured that lifts Kidd by three lifts Stockton by five or more. The stopping pin is John Stockton '90.

THE RANK GRIEVANCE IS ONLY HALF CURED AND THE NUMBER SAYS SO. The ruling's case was that Kidd '99 read ELEVENTH among 1999 point guards, under Nick Van Exel '99 (67), Rod Strickland '99 (68), Terrell Brandon '99 (72) and Stephon Marbury '99 (77). He now reads NINTH, because the change lifts his whole class with him: Van Exel '99 67 -> 71 (LEVEL with the subject, not below him), Strickland '99 68 -> 72, Brandon '99 72 -> 75, Marbury '99 77 -> 79. Kidd '02 moves 13th -> 12th among 2002 point guards (Van Exel '02 74 -> 75, Andre Miller '02 78 -> 81). Those men are inside the same term on the same bars — Strickland '99 is playvol 96 to Kidd's 94 — so no formula change inside this term can separate them; what separates Kidd from them on the card is his DEF 93, which this round does not touch. If he wants Kidd ABOVE that group on OFF rather than level with it, the lever is the o_score weights themselves (volume 0.26 against playvol 0.19), which recal_91 and recal_98 both measured and both DECLINED.

ABOVE VOLUME 30 THE EFFICIENCY FACTOR IS NOW INERT. 929 of the 1,235 cards in this term's class sit at or above PD_E_V_FULL, so for three quarters of the class the term is creation x gate x load and recal_176's PD_E_LO / PD_E_HI ramp decides nothing. That is the doctrine's own consequence — a conversion percentile is read at the load that produced it, and a man carrying the class's own quarter-load has already had his conversion priced by the standard path (efficiency at 0.11 and the signature term at 0.08 x max(volume, 50, hub load) x efficiency) — but it is a large structural claim and a later round reopening the factor should start from it.

THE SCOUT'S SENTENCE IS THE DIAGNOSIS AND IT VERIFIES. 'The efficiency factor floors at 0.5 for every lead distributor at or below the class median while the volume gate halves it again for a passer who also scores.' Both halves are true on these cards and the FIRST is the one that can move: recal_109 cut the 0.5 floor for a man who takes almost no shots ('a pure non-scorer who is also inefficient still keeps half the term, because his ruling is about the ball he moves, not about his jumper') and located it on Mark Jackson '98, volume 12. It was then paid at the same 0.5 to a man at volume 38 and a man at volume 63, whose own shot the standard path has already priced twice — efficiency at 0.11, and the signature term at 0.08 x max(volume, 50, hub load) x efficiency.

THE CUT IS recal_184's OWN MEASUREMENT USED A SECOND TIME. recal_184 established the doctrine for this term — 'the lift ABOVE THE FLOOR is paid pro rata to the man's own scoring load' — up to PD_E_V_FULL, 'the class's OWN LOWER QUARTILE of volume... exactly 30.0 under every convention'. The floor itself was the one rate in the term still read at no load at all. It now rises from 0.5 to 1.0 across the SAME class's p10 -> p25, 16 -> 30, re-measured this round on the current pool (1,235 cards: p5 10, p10 16.0, p20 26, p25 30.0, p50 52, p75 74) and already written down in recal_184's own comment. No new arbitrary constant; recal_176's ramp, recal_109's floor value, recal_117's two gates, recal_130's minute line and the size 0.245 are all untouched.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS PROVABLY WRONG, MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE KNOB. Raising PD_E_FLOOR flat was swept 0.50 / 0.60 / 0.65 / 0.70 / 0.75 / 0.80 / 0.90 / 1.00 on the full pipeline: it pays Mark Jackson '98 MORE than it pays Kidd '99 at every setting, because Jackson's gate is 0.976 against Kidd's 0.663 and his playvol is 98 against 94. At 0.80 Kidd '99 is still 68 and Jackson is on his band's top edge at 58; at 0.90 all three Mark Jackson pins fail and Kidd '99 is 70; at 1.00 — the whole factor removed — Kidd reaches 71 and Jackson reads 62, seven outside. The flat floor cannot separate the two men the ruling's own bracket names. A volume-ramped floor separates them BY CONSTRUCTION: Jackson is under the foot and moves by exactly zero.

WHAT IT PROVABLY DOES NOT TOUCH, AND IT IS EVERY PIN THIS TERM HAS EVER BEEN CUT AGAINST. Every efficient distributor is byte-identical because his factor was ALREADY 1.00 — Stockton '90 (efficiency 94) 85, Nash '05 (96) 90, Kevin Johnson '89 (79) 81, '92 (76) 82, Billups '06 (92) 92, Magic '90 (99) 93. Every pure non-scorer is byte-identical because he is at or under the foot — Mark Jackson '98 (volume 12) 52, '99 (10) 52, '00 (10) 57, and 126 of the 1,235 class cards at volume <= 16. Every lead scorer is byte-identical because recal_117's gate already pays him nothing — Harden '19, LeBron '13, Luka '23, Westbrook '15, Curry '16, SGA '25, Jordan '89.
